name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
  release:
    # `published` covers publishing a draft; `prereleased` does not fire for draft publishes.
    # `released` covers promoting an existing pre-release, which is not a publish. Publishing a
    # full release emits both, so the guard on `version` and `validate` drops the `published`
    # half and leaves the `released` run as the only one that reaches production.
    types:
      - published
      - released
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: Application version to use when publishing the project
        required: false

permissions: {}

# Queue, never cancel, outside of PRs: a cancelled run can leave an environment half-deployed
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# Note that as much as we'd love to avoid repetitive work, splitting the pipeline into separate jobs
# makes it very difficult to share artifacts between them. Even if we succeed, we'll still end up
# pushing and pulling gigabytes worth of data, which makes the jobs so much slower that we might as
# well just repeat the checkout-restore-build steps instead.

# Having a setup that involves separate jobs gives us significant benefits, on the other hand, namely:
# - Most of the jobs can run in parallel, which reduces the overall execution time significantly,
#   despite the repetitive work.
# - We can catch more issues this way, for example if the formatting job fails, we can still see the
#   the test results too.
# - If one of the jobs fails due to reasons unrelated to our code (e.g. NuGet server is down), we get
#   the option to rerun only that job, saving us time.
# - It's easier to understand what each job does (and later, read its output) because the scope is much
#   more narrow.
# - We can set permissions on a more granular (per-job) level, which allows us to expose only a few select
#   steps to more sensitive access scopes.

jobs:
  # Resolve the version from Directory.Build.props (see _version.yml)
  version:
    name: Determine version
    # A full release publish emits both `published` and `released`; skipping the `published`
    # half keeps every release transition resolving to exactly one executing run.
    if: ${{ !(github.event.action == 'published' && github.event.release.prerelease == false) }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_version.yml
    permissions:
      contents: read
    with:
      version-override: ${{ inputs.version || '' }}

  # Format and test gate (see _test.yml)
  validate:
    name: Validate
    # A full release publish emits both `published` and `released`; skipping the `published`
    # half keeps every release transition resolving to exactly one executing run.
    if: ${{ !(github.event.action == 'published' && github.event.release.prerelease == false) }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_test.yml
    permissions:
      checks: write
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    with:
      report-results: true

  # Publish the apps
  pack:
    name: Pack apps
    needs: version

    strategy:
      matrix:
        app:
          - Api
          - AdminConsole

    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: read

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@a98b56852c35b8e3190ac28c8c2271da59106c68 # v6.0.0

      - name: Install NodeJS
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: lts/*

      - name: Publish app
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          APP: ${{ matrix.app }}
        run: >
          dotnet publish "src/${APP}/"
          -p:Version="${VERSION}"
          --configuration Release
          --runtime win-x86
          --no-self-contained
          --output "src/${APP}/publish/"

      - name: Upload artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.app }}
          path: src/${{ matrix.app }}/publish/

  # Environments promote in order: devtest on every merge, qa on any release, prod only once
  # qa has deployed successfully. `trigger-actions` blocks until each deployment is terminal,
  # so `needs` is a real gate rather than just an ordering hint.
  deploy-devtest:
    name: Deploy to devtest
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
    needs:
      - version
      - validate
      - pack
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_request-deploy.yml
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    secrets:
      AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      AZURE_TENANT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
      AZURE_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
    with:
      environment: devtest
      version: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}

  deploy-qa:
    name: Deploy to QA
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'release' }}
    needs:
      - version
      - validate
      - pack
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_request-deploy.yml
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    secrets:
      AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      AZURE_TENANT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
      AZURE_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
    with:
      environment: qa
      version: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}

  deploy-prod:
    name: Deploy to production
    # `released` is the only type that marks a release as full, and the guard on `version`
    # ensures it is the only run that reaches here when a full release is published.
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'release' && github.event.action == 'released' }}
    needs:
      - version
      - deploy-qa
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_request-deploy.yml
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    secrets:
      AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      AZURE_TENANT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
      AZURE_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
    with:
      environment: prod
      version: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}

name: Request Deploy

# Requests a deployment by creating a deployment event on bitwarden/deploy, which routes the
# task through trigger-actions.yml to deploy-passwordless-server.yml and reports status back.
# The trigger blocks until the deployment reaches a terminal state, so a caller can chain
# environments with `needs:` to get a real promotion gate.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: Deployment environment (devtest, qa, prod)
        required: true
        type: string
      version:
        description: Version being deployed
        required: true
        type: string
    secrets:
      AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID:
        required: true
      AZURE_TENANT_ID:
        required: true
      AZURE_CLIENT_ID:
        required: true

permissions: {}

jobs:
  request-deploy:
    name: Request deploy to ${{ inputs.environment }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      id-token: write

    steps:
      - name: Trigger deployment
        uses: bitwarden/gh-actions/trigger-actions@main
        with:
          azure_subscription_id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
          azure_tenant_id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          azure_client_id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          task: deploy-passwordless-server
          # Artifact names match the `pack` matrix in ci.yml
          data: '{"environment": "${{ inputs.environment }}", "version": "${{ inputs.version }}", "api-artifact": "Api", "admin-console-artifact": "AdminConsole"}'

name: Validate

# Format and test gate, shared by `CI` and `Docker` so that nothing -- App Service package
# or container image -- can publish from a commit whose tests failed.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      report-results:
        description: Publish the test report check run and upload coverage
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

env:
  # Setting these variables allows .NET CLI to use rich color codes in console output
  TERM: xterm
  DOTNET_SYSTEM_CONSOLE_ALLOW_ANSI_COLOR_REDIRECTION: true
  # Skip boilerplate output
  DOTNET_SKIP_FIRST_TIME_EXPERIENCE: true
  DOTNET_NOLOGO: true
  DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT: true

permissions: {}

jobs:
  format:
    name: Validate format
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: read

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@a98b56852c35b8e3190ac28c8c2271da59106c68 # v6.0.0

      - name: Validate format
        run: dotnet format --verify-no-changes

  test:
    name: Run tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      checks: write
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install .NET
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@a98b56852c35b8e3190ac28c8c2271da59106c68 # v6.0.0

      - name: Run restore
        run: dotnet restore

      - name: Run build
        run: >
          dotnet build
          --no-restore
          --configuration Release

      - name: Run tests
        id: tests
        # Deferred so the report and coverage still publish on failure; `Fail on test failure`
        # below re-raises it. The reporter only runs for same-repo PRs, so it cannot be the
        # thing that enforces the gate on push and release builds.
        continue-on-error: true
        run: >
          dotnet test
          --no-restore
          --no-build
          --configuration Release
          --logger "trx;LogFileName=pw-test-results.trx"
          --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage"
          --
          RunConfiguration.CollectSourceInformation=true
          DataCollectionRunSettings.DataCollectors.DataCollector.Configuration.Format=opencover
        env:
          ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: Development # For Serilog passthrough

      - name: Report test results
        uses: dorny/test-reporter@a43b3a5f7366b97d083190328d2c652e1a8b6aa2 # v3.0.0
        if: ${{ inputs.report-results && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository && !cancelled() }}
        with:
          name: Test Results
          path: "**/*-test-results.trx"
          reporter: dotnet-trx
          fail-on-error: true

      - name: Upload to codecov.io
        if: ${{ inputs.report-results }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1

      - name: Fail on test failure
        if: ${{ steps.tests.outcome == 'failure' }}
        run: |
          echo "::error::Tests failed"
          exit 1

            EmailValidationErrorCode.AddressTooLong, null, null },

    new List<object[]>

# Server

This is the API server that controls FIDO2 authentication and stores credentials.

# Requirements
- [.NET 7 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download).
  - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/install/
- Database (one of the following):
  - Sqlite:
    - (do nothing)
  - Microsoft SQL Server
    - [Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/_/microsoft-mssql-server)
      - [Rosetta](https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT211861) is required for Apple M1 or newer.
    - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/sql-server/sql-server-downloads

# Getting started
1. (optional) Clone the repository.
2. (optional) Open the project in your favorite IDE.
3. (optional) Under `src/API`, edit `appsettings.Development.json`.
4. Now it's time to setup our database.
   1. We are using Sqlite by default with file name being `passwordless_dev.db`. If you specify for example a database connection string for the key `ConnectionStrings:sqlite`, then SQlite would be used. For Microsoft SQL Server you can use `ConnectionStrings:mssql`.
   2. Run the `API` project.
   3. In your browser, visit `http://localhost:7001` to execute the database migrations.

## Configuration

```json5
{
  "SALT_TOKEN": "<required base64>",
  "ConnectionStrings": {
    "mssql":"",
    "sqlite":""
  }
}
```
